class urllib3.util.Timeout(_total\=None_, _connect\=\_TYPE\_DEFAULT.token_, _read\=\_TYPE\_DEFAULT.token_)[¶](#urllib3.util.Timeout "Link to this definition")

Bases: [object](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#object "(in Python v3.14)")

Timeout configuration.

Timeouts can be defined as a default for a pool:

import urllib3

timeout = urllib3.util.Timeout(connect=2.0, read=7.0)

http = urllib3.PoolManager(timeout=timeout)

resp = http.request("GET", "https://example.com/")

print(resp.status)

Or per-request (which overrides the default for the pool):

response = http.request("GET", "https://example.com/", timeout=Timeout(10))

Timeouts can be disabled by setting all the parameters to `None`:

no_timeout = Timeout(connect=None, read=None)
response = http.request("GET", "https://example.com/", timeout=no_timeout)

Parameters:

* **total** ([_int_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int "(in Python v3.14)")_,_ [_float_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float "(in Python v3.14)")_, or_ _None_) –  
This combines the connect and read timeouts into one; the read timeout will be set to the time leftover from the connect attempt. In the event that both a connect timeout and a total are specified, or a read timeout and a total are specified, the shorter timeout will be applied.  
Defaults to None.
* **connect** ([_int_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int "(in Python v3.14)")_,_ [_float_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float "(in Python v3.14)")_, or_ _None_) – The maximum amount of time (in seconds) to wait for a connection attempt to a server to succeed. Omitting the parameter will default the connect timeout to the system default, probably [the global default timeout in socket.py](http://hg.python.org/cpython/file/603b4d593758/Lib/socket.py#l535). None will set an infinite timeout for connection attempts.
* **read** ([_int_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int "(in Python v3.14)")_,_ [_float_](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float "(in Python v3.14)")_, or_ _None_) –  
The maximum amount of time (in seconds) to wait between consecutive read operations for a response from the server. Omitting the parameter will default the read timeout to the system default, probably [the global default timeout in socket.py](http://hg.python.org/cpython/file/603b4d593758/Lib/socket.py#l535). None will set an infinite timeout.

Note

Many factors can affect the total amount of time for urllib3 to return an HTTP response.

For example, Python’s DNS resolver does not obey the timeout specified on the socket. Other factors that can affect total request time include high CPU load, high swap, the program running at a low priority level, or other behaviors.

In addition, the read and total timeouts only measure the time between read operations on the socket connecting the client and the server, not the total amount of time for the request to return a complete response. For most requests, the timeout is raised because the server has not sent the first byte in the specified time. This is not always the case; if a server streams one byte every fifteen seconds, a timeout of 20 seconds will not trigger, even though the request will take several minutes to complete.

# Retry-After header

The HTTP **`Retry-After`** [response header](/en-US/docs/Glossary/Response_header) indicates how long the user agent should wait before making a follow-up request. There are three main cases this header is used:

-   In a [`503 Service Unavailable`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/503) response, this indicates how long the service is expected to be unavailable.
-   In a [`429 Too Many Requests`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/429) response, this indicates how long to wait before making a new request.
-   In a redirect response, such as [`301 Moved Permanently`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/301), this indicates the minimum time that the user agent is asked to wait before issuing the redirected request.

## [Syntax](#syntax)

http

```
Retry-After: <http-date>
Retry-After: <delay-seconds>
```

## [Directives](#directives)

[`<http-date>`](#http-date)

A date after which to retry. See the [`Date`](/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Date) header for more details on the HTTP date format.

[`<delay-seconds>`](#delay-seconds)

A non-negative decimal integer indicating the seconds to delay after the response is received.

## [Examples](#examples)

### [Dealing with scheduled downtime](#dealing_with_scheduled_downtime)

Support for the `Retry-After` header on both clients and servers is still inconsistent. However, some crawlers and spiders, like the Googlebot, honor the `Retry-After` header. It is useful to send it along with a `503` response, so that search engines will keep indexing your site when the downtime is over.

http

```
Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT
Retry-After: 120
```

## Production Python HTTP Client Retry Policy

### When Automatic Retries Are Unsafe

Retries are unsafe whenever the request body may have reached the server. urllib3 documents that `read` errors occur "after the request was sent to the server, so the request may have side-effects" ([urllib3.util.Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry), `read` parameter). Similarly, `other` errors "might be raised after the request was sent to the server, so the request might have side-effects" ([urllib3.util.Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry), `other` parameter). In the order-creation scenario, a timeout after the body was transmitted means the order may already exist; retrying without an idempotency key risks a duplicate order. By contrast, `connect` errors are "raised before the request is sent" and are safe to retry ([urllib3.util.Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry), `connect` parameter).

### What an Idempotency Key Changes

MDN documents the `Idempotency-Key` request header, which lets the server deduplicate retries and return the original result without creating a second resource ([MDN Idempotency-Key](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Idempotency-Key)). With a key, a retried POST becomes semantically idempotent: the server either creates the order once or returns the existing one. Without it, a retried POST is a second order.

### Both Forms of Retry-After and Past Dates

MDN specifies two forms ([MDN Retry-After](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Retry-After)):

1. **`Retry-After: <delay-seconds>`** — a non-negative integer of seconds to wait after receiving the response.
2. **`Retry-After: <http-date>`** — an absolute HTTP-date after which to retry (e.g., `Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT`).

If the http-date is in the past, the client should retry immediately (zero wait). If the delay-seconds value is zero, also retry immediately.

### Why an Elapsed-Time Deadline Needs a Monotonic Clock

A 12-second elapsed-time budget must use `time.monotonic()` (Python stdlib) because wall-clock time (`time.time()`) can jump backward due to NTP adjustments, daylight saving, or manual changes, causing a retry to appear within budget when it has actually exceeded the real elapsed time. `time.monotonic()` is guaranteed non-decreasing.

### urllib3 Retry Default `allowed_methods` and POST

urllib3's default is `DEFAULT_ALLOWED_METHODS = frozenset({'DELETE', 'GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PUT', 'TRACE'})` ([urllib3.util.Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry.DEFAULT_ALLOWED_METHODS)). **`POST` is not in this set.** The docs state: "By default, we only retry on methods which are considered to be idempotent" ([urllib3.util.Retry](https://urllib3.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/urllib3.util.html#urllib3.util.Retry), `allowed_methods` parameter).

**Claim "urllib3 retries POST by default" is false.** POST is explicitly excluded from the default allowed set. To retry POST, you must pass `allowed_methods=['POST', ...]` or `allowed_methods=None` to retry on any verb.

### Bounded Retry Decision (Pseudocode)

```python
import time, http.client
from urllib3.util import Retry

def create_order(order_data, idempotency_key):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 12.0          # 12s budget, monotonic
    retry_cfg = Retry(
        total=3,
        allowed_methods=["POST"],                # POST is NOT default
        status_forcelist=[429, 503],
        backoff_factor=0.5,
        backoff_jitter=0.1,
        respect_retry_after_header=True,
    )
    attempts = 0
    while True:
        conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection(host, timeout=4)
        conn.request("POST", path, body=order_data,
                     headers={"Idempotency-Key": idempotency_key})
        try:
            resp = conn.getresponse()
        except http.client.HTTPException:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise
            attempts += 1
            if attempts >= retry_cfg.total:
                raise
            retry_cfg.sleep()
            continue

        if resp.status == 429:
            retry_after = resp.getheader("Retry-After")
            if retry_after:
                try:
                    wait = float(retry_after)          # delay-seconds
                except ValueError:
                    # http-date form: parse, clamp past dates to 0
                    wait = max(0, parse_http_date(retry_after) - time.time())
                wait = min(wait, retry_cfg.retry_after_max)
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                sleep_time = min(wait, remaining)
                if sleep_time <= 0:
                    break                             # budget exhausted
                time.sleep(sleep_time)
            else:
                retry_cfg.sleep()                     # exponential backoff
        elif resp.status >= 500:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                break
            attempts += 1
            if attempts >= retry_cfg.total:
                break
            retry_cfg.sleep()
        else:
            return resp                               # success / client error
```

**Key distinctions from urllib3 defaults:** The policy explicitly adds `POST` to `allowed_methods` (not in the default), sets `status_forcelist=[429, 503]` (default is `None`, no retries on status codes), adds `backoff_factor=0.5` with jitter (default is 0, no backoff), and enforces an absolute monotonic deadline (urllib3 has no built-in elapsed-time cap).
